# Git aliases: short commands that stay in Git

After this page you can define Git aliases with `git config`, tell them apart from shell aliases, keep a small non-destructive starter set, and know when an alias must run through the shell with `!`.

## Thesis

Long flags invite typos and discourage useful defaults. A **Git alias** is an `alias.<name>` entry in your config. Git expands it before parsing the rest of the command line, so `git lg` behaves like a built-in — and travels with your synced `~/.gitconfig`.

Verified with **git 2.47.3**.

## Mental model

```text
  typed:   git lg --all
              │
              ▼
  alias.lg = log --oneline --decorate --graph
              │
              ▼
  runs:    git log --oneline --decorate --graph --all
```

Extra arguments after the alias name are appended. That is why `git lg -5` works when the alias already includes `-n 5` only if you design the expansion without conflicting flags — prefer leaving numeric limits off the alias and passing them when needed.

| Kind | Stored in | Extra args |
|------|-----------|------------|
| Git alias | `alias.*` in config | Appended by Git |
| Shell alias / function | `~/.bashrc` | You write `"$@"` |
| Git `!` alias | config value starts with `!` | Shell sees them if you forward `"$@"` |

## Lab

<!-- file: alias-lab.sh -->
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
rm -rf /tmp/alias-demo && mkdir /tmp/alias-demo && cd /tmp/alias-demo
git init -b main
git config user.name t
git config user.email t@t
git config alias.st 'status -sb'
git config alias.lg 'log --oneline --decorate --graph -n 5'
git config alias.unstage 'reset HEAD --'
git commit --allow-empty -m base
git commit --allow-empty -m two
git config --get-regexp '^alias\.'
git st
git lg
```

Verified output on the authoring box:

```text
alias.st status -sb
alias.lg log --oneline --decorate --graph -n 5
alias.unstage reset HEAD --
=== git st ===
## main
?? out.txt
=== git lg ===
* f323fd4 (HEAD -> main) two
* e34675c base
```

## Starter set worth keeping

| Alias | Expansion | Purpose |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| `st` | `status -sb` | Compact branch + dirty paths |
| `co` | `checkout` | Short checkout (or prefer `switch`) |
| `br` | `branch` | List / create branches |
| `lg` | `log --oneline --decorate --graph` | Readable history |
| `last` | `log -1 HEAD` | Inspect tip |
| `unstage` | `reset HEAD --` | Unstage without discarding worktree |
| `diffc` | `diff --cached` | Review the index |
| `amend` | `commit --amend --no-edit` | Fold into tip (**local branches only**) |

Shell form when you need pipes:

```bash
git config --global alias.tags '!git tag -l | sort -V'
```

## Global vs local

```bash
git config --global alias.st 'status -sb'   # all repositories
git config alias.ci 'commit -v'             # this repository only
```

Repository values override globals for the same name. Audit with:

```bash
git config --get-regexp '^alias\.'
```

## Pitfalls

1. **Aliasing force-push or hard reset.** Never hide destructive defaults behind a cute name.
2. **Broken quoting.** Multi-word expansions need quotes in the config value.
3. **Documenting aliases in team runbooks.** Scripts and CI should use full commands so clones without your config still work.
4. **Shell `alias git=...` wrappers.** Debug with `type git` and `\git status`.

## Summary

- Git aliases expand before argument parsing and append extra flags.
- Keep a small, safe starter set; sync via global config or dotfiles.
- Use `!` only when you need the shell.
- Do not hide force or hard-reset behind aliases.


## Worked scenarios

### Scenario A — review before push
You want a one-liner that shows branch, dirty paths, and the last five commits:

```bash
git config --global alias.rw '!git status -sb && git log --oneline -5'
git rw
```

The `!` form runs a shell so you can chain commands. Keep it read-only.

### Scenario B — safe amend alias
Only amend when the tip is not pushed:

```bash
git config --global alias.fixup '!git log -1 --format=%an | grep -q "$GIT_AUTHOR_NAME" && git commit --amend --no-edit'
```

Even then, prefer typing `commit --amend` when sharing a branch.

### Scenario C — discover what an alias expands to
```bash
git config --get alias.lg
git help lg    # often fails — aliases are not help topics
type git       # ensure no shell wrapper
```

## Commands reference

| Goal | Command |
|------|---------|
| Set global alias | `git config --global alias.NAME 'expansion'` |
| Set repo alias | `git config alias.NAME 'expansion'` |
| List aliases | `git config --get-regexp '^alias\.'` |
| Remove alias | `git config --global --unset alias.NAME` |
| Shell alias | `git config alias.NAME '!command with "$@"'` |

## Common mistakes (extended)

- Putting spaces around `=` in older docs (`alias.st = status`) — modern `git config` wants `alias.st status` as argv pieces; quoting a single string is clearest: `git config alias.st 'status -sb'`.
- Expecting aliases to work inside `git -C otherrepo` differently — they read that repo's config plus global.
- Nested aliases calling each other deeply — keep the graph shallow for debuggability.
